---
title: "Beyond Downloading"
subtitle: "Automating data retrieval with APIs and web scraping: a practical guide for biomedical and public health researchers"
toc: false
---

Welcome! Most research data starts with someone clicking **Download**. This course shows you how to get data with code instead, so your data pulls are **reproducible**, **easy to update**, and **documented**. You will request data from public health and biomedical **APIs** (PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, openFDA, CDC, the Census), and **scrape** data from web pages when there is no API.

All examples are in **R**. The dynamic web scraping example also uses **Python** (Playwright).

## What you'll learn

-   Explain what an API is, and why researchers prefer APIs over scraping
-   Make API requests and turn JSON responses into analysis-ready tables in R
-   Use public health and biomedical APIs, including ones that need a key (the Census API)
-   Decide when web scraping is appropriate, and follow the rules (`robots.txt`, Terms of Service)
-   Scrape static HTML tables with `rvest`, using XPaths and CSS selectors
-   Recognize when a page needs a real browser (dynamic scraping), and automate one with Playwright
-   Record provenance (what you requested, when, and from where) so others can reproduce your data pull

## Start here

1.  **[Setup](pages/setup.qmd)**: install R and the packages, get a Census API key, and download the course folder. Please do this **before** the first session.
2.  **Work through the lessons in order:**

::: lesson-list
| \# | Lesson | You will learn |
|----|--------|----------------|
| 1 | [APIs](pages/lessons/01-apis.qmd) | requests, JSON, `httr`/`httr2`, NHANES, PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, openFDA, CDC (Socrata), Census |
| 2 | [Web scraping](pages/lessons/02-web-scraping.qmd) | `robots.txt`, the DOM, XPaths, `rvest`, static vs dynamic scraping, Playwright |
:::

## How each session works

1.  **🖥️ Slides**: the concepts, the rules, and a tour of the data sources. Every lesson page links to its slides, and you can download them.
2.  **👀 Live demo**: the instructor runs the demo code step by step, and you run the same code in your own copy of the demo file.

::: callout-tip
## Learning on your own?

You can! Each lesson page links to the slides and the full demo code. Download the demo file and run it one chunk at a time in R.
:::
